text: dsh-terminal-theme 是 DSH 网页端的终端配色插件，在设置页提供主题选择和导入界面，并将颜色样式限定在右侧终端面板。用户可以切换 Dracula、Nord 等内置配色，导入 JSON 或文件形式的自定义主题，复制当前主题，并随时恢复跟随应用主题。自定义主题与选择保存在当前浏览器中；无需额外密钥或外部服务。

dsh-terminal-theme adds a Settings page for choosing palettes in the DSH web client. Colors are scoped to the right sidebar terminal. Users can select built-in themes, import JSON or files, and restore the app theme. Custom themes stay in the browser; no API key or external service is required.
想只改 DSH 侧边栏终端的颜色，不影响其他界面。
能不能给终端导入自己的 ANSI 配色方案？
I want to switch my terminal panel to a custom color palette and restore the app theme later.
dsh-terminal-theme 的功能「切换终端配色」：在 Settings 页面选择内置或自定义主题后，插件只为右侧终端面板应用颜色；选择跟随应用主题可恢复默认配色。
dsh-terminal-theme 的功能「导入和管理自定义主题」：用户可粘贴 JSON 或选择 JSON 文件导入主题，插件校验颜色字段并保存到当前浏览器；页面还可复制当前主题 JSON 或删除自定义主题。

dsh-terminal-theme README · dsh-terminal-theme：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Color themes for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) terminal panel: choose a built-in palette, or import your own from JSON. The colors apply to the terminal only — the rest of DSH keeps the active theme.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Features：- **Terminal-only colors.** Every rule is scoped to the terminal panel, so the sidebar, the conversation, and Settings still read the DSH theme tokens.
- **Independent of light and dark.** A terminal theme keeps its colors when the application switches scheme.
- **Importable palettes.** Paste JSON or load a `.json` file; themes are validated, normalized, and stored in the browser.
- **Fully reversible.** Pick "Follow app theme" and the terminal returns to the stock DSH appearance; nothing else is touched.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Install：The native **Plugins** page installs it: **Add plugin** → paste a spec → **Install**. Three specs work:

| Spec | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-terminal-theme` | Once the package is published to npm |
| `https://github.com/wnanbei/dsh-terminal-theme` | Straight from GitHub; pnpm clones the repository, and there is no build step |
| `/Users/wnanbei/code/dsh-terminal-theme` | From a local clone you keep editing (installs a `link:` dependency) |

dsh-terminal-theme README · Install：The dialog also takes a tarball, a `git+https://…` address, and a different registry for that one install. It refuses a package that declares no bundle patch, so the repository root must stay a complete package.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Install：A local-directory install links the folder into the active profile (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-terminal-theme`), so later edits in that clone take effect on the next page reload without repacking. A GitHub install copies the package into the profile instead, so updating means removing and re-adding it. Either way an existing installation is reported as already installed — remove the bundle first to switch sources.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Install：```bash
git clone https://github.com/wnanbei/dsh-terminal-theme.git
```

> Agents use the same operation: `plugin_manager` `install_bundle` with one of these specs.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Usage：1. Open the terminal panel in the right sidebar, then go to **Settings → Terminal colors**.
2. Pick a card under **Color themes**; the terminal repaints immediately.
3. Pick **Follow app theme** to restore the default, including the light/dark switch.

Importing a theme:

dsh-terminal-theme README · Usage：- Paste JSON into **Import a theme** and press **Import and apply**, or press **Import from file** to load a `.json` file.
- **Fill template** writes a complete, directly editable example.
- **Copy current theme** exports the active palette; rename it and import it back to create a variant.
- The `×` on a custom theme card deletes it.

Themes live in the browser (`localStorage`), not in the profile configuration, so they survive DSH upgrades and stay out of other browsers.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Theme JSON format：```json
{
  "name": "My Theme",
  "background": "#101216",
  "foreground": "#d5dae2",

dsh-terminal-theme README · Theme JSON format：| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Display name, 1–60 characters |
| `background` / `foreground` | yes | Terminal background and default text color |
| `cursor` | no | Cursor color; defaults to `foreground` |
| `selection` | no | Selection fill; defaults to `foreground` at 30% |
| `ansi` | yes | 16 colors: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, then the 8 bright variants. 8 colors are accepted too and reused for the bright half |
| `extended` | no | Up to 240 colors for indexes 16–255 of the 256-color palette |

dsh-terminal-theme README · Theme JSON format：Colors must be hexadecimal (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`, normalized to lowercase `#rrggbb`); anything else is rejected on import with the reason shown on the page.

dsh-terminal-theme README · How it works：- All rules are scoped to the `[data-sidebar-terminal]` subtree: `--dsw-alias-bg-base` and `--dsw-alias-label-primary` are rebound there, and the xterm DOM renderer's `.xterm-fg-N` / `.xterm-bg-N` rules are overridden. No global DSH theme token changes.
- The plugin neither replaces nor wraps the terminal component, and never reads or writes its private state. Deselecting a theme only removes the injected stylesheet.
- The terminal's own OSC color handling, contrast adjustment, and cursor visibility logic keep working as before.
- Another built-in theme needs one entry in `BUILTINS` in `client.js`; anything else can go through the Settings page.
dsh-terminal-theme README · Built-in themes：Dracula, Nord, Solarized Dark / Light, Gruvbox Dark, One Dark, Tokyo Night, Catppuccin Mocha, GitHub Light.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Development：```
client.js   browser half: scoped palette stylesheet + Settings page
index.js    host half: inert, only registers the bundle row
locale/     display name and description for the plugin manager
icon.svg    plugin icon

Reload the page after editing `client.js`: the plugin manager's install record points at this directory, so no reinstall is needed.

dsh-terminal-theme README · Releasing：Versions follow Semantic Versioning: a **major** bump when the theme JSON schema or an existing built-in id changes incompatibly, a **minor** bump for new palettes or Settings features, a **patch** bump for fixes.

`version` in `package.json` is the only source of truth, and the tag is `v<version>`:

```bash
node scripts/check.mjs                      # the preflight CI runs
npm version patch -m "chore(release): v%s"  # or minor / major
git push --follow-tags
```

dsh-terminal-theme README · Releasing：Pushing the tag runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which refuses a tag that disagrees with `package.json`, re-runs the checks, packs the plugin, and publishes a GitHub Release named after the tag — with the `.tgz` attached and notes generated from the commits since the previous tag.

The tarball is an install spec too, so a release can be pinned without npm:

dsh-terminal-theme README · Releasing：- `https://github.com/wnanbei/dsh-terminal-theme/releases/download/v1.2.0/dsh-terminal-theme-1.2.0.tgz` pins that release
- `https://github.com/wnanbei/dsh-terminal-theme` tracks the default branch

Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, which is the same `node scripts/check.mjs`.
